changes: p2: name normalised to 'Umāpati' (–rāja treated as royal designation), title 'mahārājādhirāja' added from the epithet string; role kept as 'other' (patron who commissioned the original composition, not reigning king of this copy)
Date: chronogram decoded tentatively (muni 7, kumada = kumuda (diggaja) 8, ku 1, vāji 7; read right to left = Śaka 1787), giving ce_approx about 1865; year field filled
place: confidence lowered; reading left un-normalised and doubts noted
notes: rewritten to explain the chronogram uncertainty and the undecoded 'nayanahutāśana'

notes: Umāpati(rāja), called mahārājādhirāja, is the patron under whom Bhaṭṭa Keśava composed (udyotita) the campū. He is not attested as the reigning king at the time of this copy. The chronogram 'munikumadakuvājiḥ' is corrupt. It is read tentatively as muni (7), kumada for kumuda, one of the elephants of the quarters (8), ku (1), vāji (7). Read right to left this gives Śaka 1787, about 1865 CE. If 'mada' is not a number word, the reading fails, so treat the year as uncertain. 'nayanahutāśana' (2, 3) in the second hemistich may encode a further date element, such as a tithi or another year figure, but the context is too corrupt to decode. 'amanaṃgaraṅgabhaṅge' (= anaṅgaraṅgabhaṅga?) may be a descriptive phrase or a Śiva-related date term, so it was not interpreted. The place 'sadvalesa pūryām' (some '…purī') is corrupt and unidentified. No scribe, commissioner or owner is named. The colophon ends the 5th stavaka.
